attacks.claim: The plan replaces the self-hostable sync server with a hosted-only proprietary backend, contradicting the README/charter promise of self-hosting and data ownership. In 5.0 legacy REST is removed and the stride-server image archived, leaving ~3,000 self-hosted instances with no path.
attacks.evidence: "the server component is available only as the hosted Cirrus Cloud service" / "Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend and the stride-server Docker image is archived."

attacks.claim: The 5.0 removal of legacy sync and archival of the server image is a one-way door for self-hosters. There is no migration path to Cirrus Cloud, no way to keep data on their own infrastructure, and no fallback if Cirrus proves unsuitable or changes terms.
attacks.evidence: "Legacy REST sync is removed in app 5.0 ... the stride-server Docker image is archived." / ABSENT: fallback or exit plan

attacks.claim: Single-vendor dependency with high exit cost for all ~90k users. The client is a closed binary and the server is vendor-only. There is no export of Cirrus-held data back to a self-owned store, and no pricing is given beyond the free tier, which is close to the 100k cap.
attacks.evidence: "free up to 100k monthly active devices; our 90k fits the free tier." / ABSENT: exit plan, post-free-tier pricing

attacks.claim: An MIT open-source app embeds a prebuilt binary SDK under a commercial license, with no license compatibility review. This may restrict redistribution, forks and F-Droid-style builds, and conflicts with the project's open-source promises.
attacks.evidence: "distributed as a prebuilt binary (iOS xcframework, Android AAR) under the Cirrus commercial license" / ABSENT: license review

attacks.claim: All workout data, including GPS tracks (home and route locations), moves to a third-party cloud. The plan states no consent or notice, data residency, or vendor retention terms, and no verification that deletion has completed. Self-hosting users opted for ownership specifically to avoid this.
attacks.evidence: "Account deletion removes the Cirrus user record and all synced records via the Cirrus admin API within 30 days." / ABSENT: consent, residency, vendor retention terms

attacks.claim: The central claim of record-level resumable uploads with no partial workouts is unprototyped, and the plan is dispatched before the week-1 spike validates it. There is no go/no-go gate after the spike.
attacks.evidence: "a dropped connection never leaves a partial workout." / "Week 1: Cirrus integration spike"

attacks.claim: The tombstone guarantee is contradicted by its own retention window. A device offline for more than 90 days can resurrect a deleted workout. Device-stamped HLCs also trust device clocks for LWW.
attacks.evidence: "Deletes are tombstones retained 90 days so an offline device cannot resurrect a deleted workout."

attacks.claim: The rollout halt criterion is crash-free sessions only. Nothing measures duplicate or lost workouts, the very problem being fixed, so a sync-correctness regression would not stop the staged rollout.
attacks.evidence: "halting if crash-free sessions drop below 99.3%." / ABSENT: duplicate/loss rollout gate

attacks.claim: Backup deletion after 30 days and two syncs depends on the unproven vendor sync. The plan does not describe how a downgrade restore is reconciled with workouts already in Cirrus, so duplicates are possible.
attacks.evidence: "the backup is deleted only after 30 days and two successful syncs."

attacks.claim: At 90k of a 100k free-tier cap, modest growth would exceed the free tier within the window before 5.0. No budget or overage plan is stated.
